speaker_title: Address by Ms. Jacinda Ardern, Prime Minister and Minister for National Security and Intelligence, Child Poverty Reduction, and Ministerial Services of New Zealand

paragraphs.text: I greet you in te reo Māori, the language of the indigenous people of Aotearoa New Zealand.
paragraphs.raw_text:
I greet you in te reo Māori, the language of the indigenous people of Aotearoa 
New Zealand.

paragraphs.text: As I deliver this address to the General Assembly from here in New Zealand, it strikes me that even when global events threaten to disconnect and divide us, a shared instinct to connect with one another, still prevails.
paragraphs.raw_text:
As I deliver this address to the General Assembly from here in New Zealand, 
it strikes me that even when global events threaten to disconnect and divide us, a 
shared instinct to connect with one another, still prevails.

paragraphs.text: I have often described New Zealand as being remote, but connected. The COVID-19 pandemic has made both parts of this statement truer than ever. In some ways, we now feel that remoteness more keenly. The vast ocean surrounding our islands have taken on an even greater significance in a time when our border controls are our first line of defence against a highly contagious, global virus.
paragraphs.raw_text:
I have often described New Zealand as being remote, but connected. The 
COVID-19 pandemic has made both parts of this statement truer than ever. In some 
ways, we now feel that remoteness more keenly. The vast ocean surrounding our 
islands have taken on an even greater significance in a time when our border controls 
are our first line of defence against a highly contagious, global virus.

paragraphs.text: Despite this physical distancing, the pandemic has demonstrated more starkly than ever just how closely connected we all are. We live in a world where domestic decisions made half a world away, are as significant to us as those made by our nearest neighbours.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Despite this physical distancing, the pandemic has demonstrated more starkly 
than ever just how closely connected we all are. We live in a world where domestic 
decisions made half a world away, are as significant to us as those made by our 
nearest neighbours.

paragraphs.text: In many ways, COVID-19 is an illustration of global transboundary problems at a local level. Here is an invisible threat, which no one is safe from, and the very thing keeping us safe — is each other. We have placed our trust in the actions of neighbours and strangers — to wear masks, to distance, to get vaccinated and support others to do so, and we live collectively with the consequences.
paragraphs.raw_text:
In many ways, COVID-19 is an illustration of global transboundary problems 
at a local level. Here is an invisible threat, which no one is safe from, and the very 
thing keeping us safe — is each other. We have placed our trust in the actions of 
neighbours and strangers — to wear masks, to distance, to get vaccinated and support 
others to do so, and we live collectively with the consequences.

paragraphs.text: It has been a privilege for me as a leader, to witness the practical application of New Zealanders’ values to these challenges.
paragraphs.raw_text:
It has been a privilege for me as a leader, to witness the practical application 
of New Zealanders’ values to these challenges.

paragraphs.text: Values like manaakitanga and whanaungatanga, which in the Māori language mean kindness, and a shared sense of humanity and connectedness. Values like kotahitanga, or a shared aspiration and unity towards a common goal.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Values like manaakitanga and whanaungatanga, which in the Māori language 
mean kindness, and a shared sense of humanity and connectedness. Values like 
kotahitanga, or a shared aspiration and unity towards a common goal.

paragraphs.text: These values have seen New Zealanders take care of one another, and work together to limit the transmission of COVID-19 in our communities.
paragraphs.raw_text:
These values have seen New Zealanders take care of one another, and work 
together to limit the transmission of COVID-19 in our communities.

paragraphs.text: Now these values are not unique to New Zealand. They are universal. They underpin the Charter of the United Nations. One need only read the preamble to see them reflected back at us.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Now these values are not unique to New Zealand. They are universal. They 
underpin the Charter of the United Nations. One need only read the preamble to see 
them reflected back at us.

paragraphs.text: No community, nation, or region acting alone can address COVID-19. It is a complex, global problem that requires a global solution. Equitable access to safe and effective vaccines for everyone is essential to our response and recovery.
paragraphs.raw_text:
No community, nation, or region acting alone can address COVID-19. It is a 
complex, global problem that requires a global solution. Equitable access to safe and 
effective vaccines for everyone is essential to our response and recovery.

paragraphs.text: New Zealand is working with others, especially Australia, to support full vaccine coverage for Pacific island countries. And the COVAX Facility is doing essential work distributing vaccines worldwide. But more must be done to support this effort. New Zealand is proud to have been amongst the first countries to donate doses to the COVAX Advance Market Commitment in addition to our financial support.
paragraphs.raw_text:
New Zealand is working with others, especially Australia, to support full 
vaccine coverage for Pacific island countries. And the COVAX Facility is doing 
essential work distributing vaccines worldwide. But more must be done to support this 
effort. New Zealand is proud to have been amongst the first countries to donate doses 
to the COVAX Advance Market Commitment in addition to our financial support.

paragraphs.text: New Zealand continues to work in WTO and APEC to support a waiver of intellectual property protections for vaccines and other measures to increase availability.
paragraphs.raw_text:
New Zealand continues to work in WTO and APEC to support a 
waiver of intellectual property protections for vaccines and other measures to 
increase availability.

paragraphs.text: Without equitable access for all, we risk further variants developing which could undermine or undo our progress.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Without equitable access for all, we risk further variants developing which 
could undermine or undo our progress.

paragraphs.text: At the same time that the direct impacts of COVID-19 have brought immeasurable pain to many across the world, it has also exacerbated and further complicated other existing global challenges. We know what these challenges are. We articulated them as areas of action in the UN Seventy-Fifth Anniversary Declaration.
paragraphs.raw_text:
At the same time that the direct impacts of COVID-19 have brought 
immeasurable pain to many across the world, it has also exacerbated and further 
complicated other existing global challenges. We know what these challenges are. We 
articulated them as areas of action in the UN Seventy-Fifth Anniversary Declaration.

paragraphs.text: The pandemic has been the ultimate disrupter. It has changed our realities, and given us cause to pause and reflect. In the disruption is an opportunity for us to reset. To adjust some of our fundamental settings to put us in a better position to respond to our shared challenges.
paragraphs.raw_text:
The pandemic has been the ultimate disrupter. It has changed our realities, and 
given us cause to pause and reflect. In the disruption is an opportunity for us to reset. 
To adjust some of our fundamental settings to put us in a better position to respond 
to our shared challenges.

paragraphs.text: We have heard so much about ‘building back better’. We must do better. Like the drafters of the Charter, we owe future generations our commitment to hand down a better world forged through cooperation.
paragraphs.raw_text:
We have heard so much about ‘building back better’. We must do better. Like 
the drafters of the Charter, we owe future generations our commitment to hand down 
a better world forged through cooperation.

paragraphs.text: Fortunately for us, we already have a blueprint for such a world in the Sustainable Development Goals, and the 2030 Agenda. The 2030 Agenda recognises that as our shared challenges are interconnected, so too must be our responses. As we face a series of interlinked global crises that demand action, now is the time for us to recommit to the SDGs.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Fortunately for us, we already have a blueprint for such a world in the 
Sustainable Development Goals, and the 2030 Agenda. The 2030 Agenda recognises 
that as our shared challenges are interconnected, so too must be our responses. As 
we face a series of interlinked global crises that demand action, now is the time for 
us to recommit to the SDGs.

paragraphs.text: COVID-19 cannot be an excuse for not achieving the SDGs. In fact, it’s a further reason why we must.
paragraphs.raw_text:
COVID-19 cannot be an excuse for not achieving the SDGs. In fact, it’s a 
further reason why we must.

paragraphs.text: There is perhaps no better example of a global crisis that demands action than climate change.
paragraphs.raw_text:
There is perhaps no better example of a global crisis that demands action than 
climate change.

paragraphs.text: Climate change is one of the most pervasive crises of our time. From rising sea levels to shifting weather patterns, the impacts are global in scope, unprecedented in scale, and happening right now.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Climate change is one of the most pervasive crises of our time. From rising sea 
levels to shifting weather patterns, the impacts are global in scope, unprecedented in 
scale, and happening right now.

paragraphs.text: Climate change touches all of our lives, but countries in the Pacific are some of the most affected, despite having contributed least to the problem. Pacific leaders view climate change as the single greatest threat to the livelihoods, security and wellbeing of the peoples of the region.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Climate change touches all of our lives, but countries in the Pacific are some 
of the most affected, despite having contributed least to the problem. Pacific leaders 
view climate change as the single greatest threat to the livelihoods, security and 
wellbeing of the peoples of the region.

paragraphs.text: Any global response that fails to limit global warming to 1.5 degrees above pre-industrial levels is unacceptable. This is our goal, and our collective efforts must achieve it. The latest science from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change is stark.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Any global response that fails to limit global warming to 1.5 degrees above 
pre-industrial levels is unacceptable. This is our goal, and our collective efforts must 
achieve it. The latest science from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change 
is stark.

paragraphs.text: The climate crisis cannot be beaten through incrementalism. The science demands that we do so much more.
paragraphs.raw_text:
The climate crisis cannot be beaten through incrementalism. The science 
demands that we do so much more.

paragraphs.text: New Zealand has made the 1.5°C limit the heart of our domestic climate change legislation. We have committed to a 2050 target and we are revising our Nationally Determined Contribution.
paragraphs.raw_text:
New Zealand has made the 1.5°C limit the heart of our domestic climate change 
legislation. We have committed to a 2050 target and we are revising our Nationally 
Determined Contribution.

paragraphs.text: As we mitigate, we must also adapt. This year New Zealand conducted its first national climate change risk assessment to tell us where to focus our effort, and within two years we will have a national adaptation plan. But we have already begun our journey. New Zealand has a programme to plant for instance, one billion trees by 2028. This will store carbon, but it will also support forest resilience, prevent erosion, improve biodiversity, and support our rural and indigenous communities.
paragraphs.raw_text:
As we mitigate, we must also adapt. This year New Zealand conducted its 
first national climate change risk assessment to tell us where to focus our effort, and 
within two years we will have a national adaptation plan. But we have already begun 
our journey. New Zealand has a programme to plant for instance, one billion trees 
by 2028. This will store carbon, but it will also support forest resilience, prevent 
erosion, improve biodiversity, and support our rural and indigenous communities.

paragraphs.text: Lifting the ambition of our nationally determined contributions is vital, but there are also collective actions we need to take.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Lifting the ambition of our nationally determined contributions is vital, but 
there are also collective actions we need to take.

paragraphs.text: This includes bringing an end to fossil fuel and other environmentally harmful subsidies. It includes pooling our resources and knowledge through the Global Research Alliance so that we can grow more food without growing emissions. It includes negotiating an agreement on climate change, trade and sustainability. New Zealand is actively pursuing all of these outcomes.
paragraphs.raw_text:
This includes bringing an end to fossil fuel and other environmentally harmful 
subsidies. It includes pooling our resources and knowledge through the Global 
Research Alliance so that we can grow more food without growing emissions. It 
includes negotiating an agreement on climate change, trade and sustainability. New 
Zealand is actively pursuing all of these outcomes.

paragraphs.text: We must collectively address the unjust and potentially destabilising consequences of climate change.
paragraphs.raw_text:
We must collectively address the unjust and potentially destabilising 
consequences of climate change.

paragraphs.text: For Small Island Developing States, one of the gravest consequences is sea-level rise. The ocean is central to the culture and livelihoods of the peoples of the Pacific. Pacific countries have also planned their economies and long-term development in reliance on the maritime zones and resources guaranteed to them under the Law of the Sea Convention.
paragraphs.raw_text:
For Small Island Developing States, one of the gravest consequences is sea-level 
rise. The ocean is central to the culture and livelihoods of the peoples of the Pacific. 
Pacific countries have also planned their economies and long-term development in 
reliance on the maritime zones and resources guaranteed to them under the Law of 
the Sea Convention.

paragraphs.text: It is only right that as an international community, we work to ensure the maintenance of those zones and rights in the face of climate change-related sealevel rise.
paragraphs.raw_text:
It is only right that as an international community, we work to ensure the 
maintenance of those zones and rights in the face of climate change-related sea-
level rise.

paragraphs.text: As a contribution to this objective, I was pleased to join my fellow Pacific Islands Forum Leaders in issuing the ‘Declaration on Preserving Maritime Zones in the Face of Climate Change-related Sea-Level Rise’, in August this year.
paragraphs.raw_text:
As a contribution to this objective, I was pleased to join my fellow Pacific 
Islands Forum Leaders in issuing the ‘Declaration on Preserving Maritime Zones in 
the Face of Climate Change-related Sea-Level Rise’, in August this year.

paragraphs.text: Climate change is closely interlinked with another crisis of a planetary scale — that of global biodiversity loss.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Climate change is closely interlinked with another crisis of a planetary scale — 
that of global biodiversity loss.

paragraphs.text: As much as we are all interconnected as nations, so too are we connected with nature and the services it provides. We depend on it for the air we breathe, and the economies we have built. Biodiversity loss threatens our well-being, our prosperity, and our health. It will both accelerate climate change, and make its impacts worse.
paragraphs.raw_text:
As much as we are all interconnected as nations, so too are we connected with 
nature and the services it provides. We depend on it for the air we breathe, and the 
economies we have built. Biodiversity loss threatens our well-being, our prosperity, 
and our health. It will both accelerate climate change, and make its impacts worse.

paragraphs.text: This is a challenge that requires us to work across barriers and silos. For New Zealand’s part, we have adopted the Aotearoa New Zealand Biodiversity Strategy
paragraphs.raw_text:
This is a challenge that requires us to work across barriers and silos. For New 
Zealand’s part, we have adopted the Aotearoa New Zealand Biodiversity Strategy

paragraphs.text: 2020 — Te Mana o te Taiao — which will guide our actions domestically for the protection, restoration and sustainable use of biodiversity.
paragraphs.raw_text:
2020 — Te Mana o te Taiao — which will guide our actions domestically for the 
protection, restoration and sustainable use of biodiversity.

paragraphs.text: We simply cannot achieve the 2030 Agenda unless we unite with collective ambition to reverse biodiversity loss by 2030. We have an opportunity to do this by adopting and implementing an ambitious and transformational post-2020 global biodiversity framework at the upcoming Conference of Parties. New Zealand is committed to this, and I urge you to join us.
paragraphs.raw_text:
We simply cannot achieve the 2030 Agenda unless we unite with collective 
ambition to reverse biodiversity loss by 2030. We have an opportunity to do this 
by adopting and implementing an ambitious and transformational post-2020 global 
biodiversity framework at the upcoming Conference of Parties. New Zealand is 
committed to this, and I urge you to join us.

paragraphs.text: As with biodiversity on land, ocean biodiversity is equally important. New Zealand looks forward to concluding the negotiations on an UN treaty for the conservation and sustainable use of high seas biodiversity.
paragraphs.raw_text:
As with biodiversity on land, ocean biodiversity is equally important. New 
Zealand looks forward to concluding the negotiations on an UN treaty for the 
conservation and sustainable use of high seas biodiversity.

paragraphs.text: But as we turn our mind to the challenges we face globally, we must turn to the most important thing of all — he tangata, he tangata, he tangata — it is people, people, people.
paragraphs.raw_text:
But as we turn our mind to the challenges we face globally, we must turn to 
the most important thing of all — he tangata, he tangata, he tangata — it is people, 
people, people.

paragraphs.text: More than 120 million people have been pushed into extreme poverty as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic. Inequality within and between countries has deepened.
paragraphs.raw_text:
More than 120 million people have been pushed into extreme poverty as a result 
of the COVID-19 pandemic. Inequality within and between countries has deepened.

paragraphs.text: These consequences were never inevitable, and there are steps we can take to reverse these trends and improve the lives of those impacted.
paragraphs.raw_text:
These consequences were never inevitable, and there are steps we can take to 
reverse these trends and improve the lives of those impacted.

paragraphs.text: Too many people go hungry every day. New Zealand invests heavily in sustainable food production, and what we produce feeds many times our own population. But we have seen that at the global level, food systems are neither sustainable nor resilient. They suffer from, and contribute to, the overlapping impacts of climate change and biodiversity loss. Transformational change is needed to ensure that everyone has access to the nutrition they need.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Too many people go hungry every day. New Zealand invests heavily in 
sustainable food production, and what we produce feeds many times our own 
population. But we have seen that at the global level, food systems are neither 
sustainable nor resilient. They suffer from, and contribute to, the overlapping impacts 
of climate change and biodiversity loss. Transformational change is needed to ensure 
that everyone has access to the nutrition they need.

paragraphs.text: This week’s Food Systems Summit is an important step, and it must be the beginning of an ongoing effort. We will do our part in supporting these efforts, including on initiatives that acknowledge the leadership of indigenous peoples in food systems and increase global ambition to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from agriculture.
paragraphs.raw_text:
This week’s Food Systems Summit is an important step, and it must be the 
beginning of an ongoing effort. We will do our part in supporting these efforts, 
including on initiatives that acknowledge the leadership of indigenous peoples in 
food systems and increase global ambition to reduce greenhouse gas emissions 
from agriculture.

paragraphs.text: For our part — this is an area where we are working hard, with a unique agreement between our food sector, government and Māori to reduce agricultural emissions through a pricing mechanism. We are determined to show the world what is possible.
paragraphs.raw_text:
For our part — this is an area where we are working hard, with a unique 
agreement between our food sector, government and Māori to reduce agricultural 
emissions through a pricing mechanism. We are determined to show the world what 
is possible.

paragraphs.text: At the same time we must include making trade more open and inclusive. COVID-19 disrupted global supply chains, while at the same time it illustrated the importance of open trade to protecting the health of people and lifting them out of poverty and hunger. We must commit to ensuring the flow of essential goods and services, and reject any temptation to turn inwards and focus on protectionism.
paragraphs.raw_text:
At the same time we must include making trade more open and inclusive. 
COVID-19 disrupted global supply chains, while at the same time it illustrated the 
importance of open trade to protecting the health of people and lifting them out of 
poverty and hunger. We must commit to ensuring the flow of essential goods and 
services, and reject any temptation to turn inwards and focus on protectionism.

paragraphs.text: We know that poverty and inequality drive conflict and instability, and we are also seeing this, in heightened civil unrest and conflict. Humanitarian crises have worsened. We are seeing this in Afghanistan and there are many more.
paragraphs.raw_text:
We know that poverty and inequality drive conflict and instability, and we are 
also seeing this, in heightened civil unrest and conflict. Humanitarian crises have 
worsened. We are seeing this in Afghanistan and there are many more.

paragraphs.text: As an international community we must rise to the challenge of meeting the growing humanitarian need. But we also have to intensify our efforts to prevent conflict and build peace. New Zealand looks forward to playing a part in this effort as we join the Peacebuilding Commission in 2022.
paragraphs.raw_text:
As an international community we must rise to the challenge of meeting the 
growing humanitarian need. But we also have to intensify our efforts to prevent 
conflict and build peace. New Zealand looks forward to playing a part in this effort 
as we join the Peacebuilding Commission in 2022.

paragraphs.text: As leaders, we have a responsibility to foster and sustain peace in our societies. We know what the necessary conditions are. Yes, this includes the absence of poverty, hunger, and material deprivation. But it is also something more. Peaceful societies are inclusive societies, where diversity is embraced and everyone has both the means and the opportunities to contribute to the fullness of their potential. Where women and girls are lifted up and encouraged to exercise their voice and their agency.
paragraphs.raw_text:
As leaders, we have a responsibility to foster and sustain peace in our societies. 
We know what the necessary conditions are. Yes, this includes the absence of poverty, 
hunger, and material deprivation. But it is also something more. Peaceful societies 
are inclusive societies, where diversity is embraced and everyone has both the means 
and the opportunities to contribute to the fullness of their potential. Where women 
and girls are lifted up and encouraged to exercise their voice and their agency.

paragraphs.text: Whatever our political or constitutional systems, no nation will ever be truly peaceful in the absence of these basic conditions, founded on the fundamental and equal rights of every person.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Whatever our political or constitutional systems, no nation will ever be truly 
peaceful in the absence of these basic conditions, founded on the fundamental and 
equal rights of every person.

paragraphs.text: And where peace fails, we must all do our part to strengthen and improve respect for the laws of armed conflict, and to enhance the protection of civilians. Preventing both the use of illegal weapons, and the illegal use of legal weapons, is essential, as is ensuring there is no impunity for any such use. This work is a shared responsibility, and one which we pursue alongside our tireless efforts to rid the world of nuclear weapons and the spectre of a conflict that no one can recover from.
paragraphs.raw_text:
And where peace fails, we must all do our part to strengthen and improve 
respect for the laws of armed conflict, and to enhance the protection of civilians. 
Preventing both the use of illegal weapons, and the illegal use of legal weapons, is 
essential, as is ensuring there is no impunity for any such use. This work is a shared 
responsibility, and one which we pursue alongside our tireless efforts to rid the world 
of nuclear weapons and the spectre of a conflict that no one can recover from.

paragraphs.text: All of these challenges we share might cause us to re-examine our response to being so interconnected. We have a choice. To approach our shared challenges from a place of fear, hoping to protect narrowly defined interests by turning inwards. Or we can reaffirm our trust in cooperation, understanding that our greatest fears can only be tackled by concerted collective action.
paragraphs.raw_text:
All of these challenges we share might cause us to re-examine our response to 
being so interconnected. We have a choice. To approach our shared challenges from a 
place of fear, hoping to protect narrowly defined interests by turning inwards. Or we 
can reaffirm our trust in cooperation, understanding that our greatest fears can only 
be tackled by concerted collective action.

paragraphs.text: Our forebears were once at this fork in the road. They chose the path of trust. They founded the United Nations.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Our forebears were once at this fork in the road. They chose the path of trust. 
They founded the United Nations.

paragraphs.text: It is times like these when we have the most to gain by reminding ourselves of what the Charter’s preamble says. It speaks to a concern for future generations. It speaks about universal observance of human rights, respect for international law, and living together in peace as good neighbours. It speaks about uniting our strength, and combining our efforts to accomplish our aims.
paragraphs.raw_text:
It is times like these when we have the most to gain by reminding ourselves 
of what the Charter’s preamble says. It speaks to a concern for future generations. It 
speaks about universal observance of human rights, respect for international law, and 
living together in peace as good neighbours. It speaks about uniting our strength, and 
combining our efforts to accomplish our aims.

paragraphs.text: These words of determination were in response to the devastation of war. They apply equally to the collective challenges we face today, and if we are to resolve these in an enduring way, we must look beyond government.
paragraphs.raw_text:
These words of determination were in response to the devastation of war. They 
apply equally to the collective challenges we face today, and if we are to resolve these 
in an enduring way, we must look beyond government.

paragraphs.text: Inclusive multilateralism is one in which our common understandings are enriched by diverse perspectives. As governments, we owe it to ourselves to be open to the expertise and partnerships offered by stakeholders, whether they are from civil society, industry, or indigenous groups.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Inclusive multilateralism is one in which our common understandings are 
enriched by diverse perspectives. As governments, we owe it to ourselves to be open 
to the expertise and partnerships offered by stakeholders, whether they are from civil 
society, industry, or indigenous groups.

paragraphs.text: I have seen in the progress we have made through the Christchurch Call to Action, what can be achieved when governments, industry, and civil society work together in a multistakeholder capacity to eliminate terrorist and violent extremist content online, and I am utterly committed to further efforts on this important work.
paragraphs.raw_text:
I have seen in the progress we have made through the Christchurch Call to 
Action, what can be achieved when governments, industry, and civil society work 
together in a multistakeholder capacity to eliminate terrorist and violent extremist 
content online, and I am utterly committed to further efforts on this important work.

paragraphs.text: New Zealand is committed to advancing Our Common Agenda, and sadly, as we have seen in recent times, an essential element of this is preparedness.
paragraphs.raw_text:
New Zealand is committed to advancing Our Common Agenda, and sadly, as 
we have seen in recent times, an essential element of this is preparedness.

paragraphs.text: No one can argue for instance that the global community as a whole was adequately prepared for a global pandemic. It is clear that we will face further global health risks, and we have no excuses for remaining unprepared.
paragraphs.raw_text:
No one can argue for instance that the global community as a whole was 
adequately prepared for a global pandemic. It is clear that we will face further global 
health risks, and we have no excuses for remaining unprepared.

paragraphs.text: New Zealand strongly supports the ambitious and practical approach of the Independent
paragraphs.raw_text:
New Zealand strongly supports the ambitious and practical approach of the 
Independent

paragraphs.text: Panel for Pandemic Preparedness and Response. We will not just passively support the Independent Panel’s recommendations. We will actively engage on work streams to develop a pandemic treaty, convention or other international instrument; to improve global surveillance, validation and early response; and importantly, to strengthen the World Health Organization.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Panel for Pandemic Preparedness and Response. We will not just passively 
support the Independent Panel’s recommendations. We will actively engage on work 
streams to develop a pandemic treaty, convention or other international instrument; 
to improve global surveillance, validation and early response; and importantly, to 
strengthen the World Health Organization.

paragraphs.text: If there is any lesson we can draw from the events of the past 18 months, it is the need for more, and better, cooperation. And with the need for better cooperation, comes the need for responsive and adaptive global institutions, including the United Nations.
paragraphs.raw_text:
If there is any lesson we can draw from the events of the past 18 months, it is 
the need for more, and better, cooperation. And with the need for better cooperation, 
comes the need for responsive and adaptive global institutions, including the 
United Nations.

paragraphs.text: I commend and thank the Secretary-General on his report and recommendations to advance Our Common Agenda. These provide us with a roadmap for a more inclusive and effective multilateralism. One that includes a voice for the needs of future generations and leaves no one behind.
paragraphs.raw_text:
I commend and thank the Secretary-General on his report and recommendations 
to advance Our Common Agenda. These provide us with a roadmap for a more 
inclusive and effective multilateralism. One that includes a voice for the needs of 
future generations and leaves no one behind.

paragraphs.text: As leaders, we have the power to shape our shared institutions and to make them fit for purpose. We must not shy away from this task.
paragraphs.raw_text:
As leaders, we have the power to shape our shared institutions and to make 
them fit for purpose. We must not shy away from this task.

paragraphs.text: I can think of no better way to reaffirm our kindness towards one another, our shared humanity, and our unity.
paragraphs.raw_text:
I can think of no better way to reaffirm our kindness towards one another, our 
shared humanity, and our unity.

paragraphs.text: I hope you will join us.
paragraphs.raw_text: I hope you will join us.

paragraphs.text: Tēnā koutou, tēnā koutou, tēnā tātou katoa.
paragraphs.raw_text: Tēnā koutou, tēnā koutou, tēnā tātou katoa.
